title: K-Search: LLM Kernel Generation via Co-Evolving Intrinsic World Model

mechanism.domainTask: GPU kernel optimization through tree-guided planning and repeated LLM code instantiation
mechanism.populationDetail: The search state is explicitly a tree of closed actions with evaluated programs and open frontier actions carrying parent-program/optimization-intent pairs and priorities.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate archive is described; best programs are attached to closed tree nodes and the best found kernel is returned.
mechanism.replacementDetail: World Model updates tree state through Insert, Update, and Prune; this action-tree maintenance is not described as population or archive replacement.
mechanism.generationDetail: The code policy instantiates a high-level optimization intent against one selected parent kernel; the intent may imply structural or local changes, with no constrained patch-only protocol.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Evaluator returns correctness, latency/performance, and compiler/profiler metadata; observations are consumed by World Model updates and inform subsequent code instantiation.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Each selected frontier action explicitly contains one parent program and one high-level intent; the World Model selects the action with maximum current priority.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A co-evolving LLM World Model maintains a search tree of high-level optimization intents, separately from the stochastic code policy that instantiates kernels.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/K-Search LLM Kernel Generation via Co-Evolving Intrinsic World Model.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently calls K-Search a tree-structured population; the paper's maintained structure is specifically an action/hypothesis tree with programs attached to closed nodes, not a conventional candidate tree. Do not attribute baseline MAP-Elites mechanisms to K-Search. Model backbone identity and replacement mapping remain unclear.
